predecessors.name: Later Han (Five Dynasties)
predecessors.text: the Northern Han realm: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: the Northern Han realm at its end: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

ledger.x: 951: Liu Min founds the Northern Han in Shanxi.
979: the Song take the Northern Han.

979: the Northern Han ends, the last of the Ten Kingdoms to fall before the Song reunified China proper (the Five Dynasties page: 'the Northern Han maintained nominal independence until the Song dynasty wrested it from the Khitans in 979').

wars.name: Battle of Gaoping
wars.outcome: Liu Chong was defeated by Chai Rong of the Later Zhou and died soon afterwards; the pages opened give no territorial result.

wars.name: Song conquest of Northern Han
wars.outcome: Taizong of Song took the capital after a two-month siege and incorporated the kingdom into the Northern Song.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Northern Han border; the realm is a small Shanxi core and its edges are approximate.

sources.title: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period
